 News › News News › CAT 2026: Admit card to be released today, check key details here CAT 2026: Admit card to be released today, check key details here
 TNN Updated: Nov 4, 2026, 09:00 IST The CAT 2026 admit card will be released today, November 4, by the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Indore. Candidates who have registered for the exam can download their hall tickets from the official CAT website.
 To access the admit card, candidates will need to log in using their user ID and password. The admit card will contain important details such as the candidate's name, photograph, registration number, exam centre, test slot, and reporting time.
 The CAT 2026 exam is scheduled to be held on November 29 at centres across India. The examination will take place in three sessions. Candidates are advised to download their admit cards as soon as they become available and verify all details carefully.
 How To Download CAT 2026 Admit Card
 Visit iimcat.ac.in .
 Click on the candidate login link.
 Enter your user ID and password.
 Submit the details.
 Your CAT 2026 admit card will appear on the screen.
 Download and save it for future reference.
 After downloading the admit card, candidates should carefully verify their personal details, photograph and signature, registration number, examination centre address, exam date and timing, and reporting time to ensure that all the information is accurate.
 Candidates must carry a printed copy of the admit card and a valid photo ID proof to the examination centre on the day of the test.
 Exam Schedule
 The examination will be conducted in three sessions:
 Slot 1: 8:30 am to 10:30 am
 Slot 2: 12:30 pm to 2:30 pm
 Slot 3: 4:30 pm to 6:30 pm
 The slot assigned to each candidate, along with the reporting time, will be mentioned on the admit card.
 Exam Pattern
 The CAT 2026 question paper will comprise 68 questions divided into three sections: Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension (VARC), Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR), and Quantitative Ability (QA). As per the marking scheme, candidates will be awarded three marks for every correct answer, while one mark will be deducted for each incorrect response.
 If any information is incorrect, candidates should immediately contact the exam authorities for assistance.
